title: Exhaustion for Metaplectic Covering Data
body_html:
Exhaustion for Metaplectic Covering Data

Let \(V'\) be a symplectic \(F\)-space of even dimension \(n\), and let \(Mp\) be the \(\mathbb C^\times\)-metaplectic cover of \(Sp(V')\). If \[ p\ge \max\{2n+3,e_F(n+1)+2\}, \] then every genuine supercuspidal representation of \(Mp\) is attached to a covering datum.
proof_html: Start with a genuine supercuspidal \(Mp\)-module \(\widetilde\pi'\). The conservation relation gives an odd-dimensional quadratic space \(V\), with \(\dim_FV\le n+1\), and a genuine supercuspidal representation \(\widetilde\pi\) on the corresponding orthogonal cover such that \[ \widetilde\pi'=\theta_{V,V'}(\widetilde\pi). \] The residue-characteristic bound puts both groups under Kim's hypotheses, so \(\widetilde\pi\) is attached to a covering datum on the odd orthogonal side. Proposition 9.1 then produces source and target data whose target attached representation is \(\widetilde\pi'\). The equivalence theorem for covering data identifies the source datum with the original one, so the target representation is attached to the constructed metaplectic datum.
